subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve default parallel distinct ACP session launches and fix launch readiness, or add a per-backend/agent concurrency gate for ACPX/Claude?
rationale: Current code and tests preserve distinct ACP session parallelism, while a broad default serialization fix would change existing behavior without proving the actual launch failure boundary.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and require live proof
options.body: Keep default distinct-session parallelism and require a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude reproduction before choosing an OpenClaw or ACPX readiness fix.

options.title: Add an opt-in concurrency gate
options.body: Use the existing or a narrower explicit concurrency setting for operators who need serialization without changing default behavior.

options.title: Serialize ACPX/Claude by default
options.body: Make rapid distinct-session launches wait by default, accepting the compatibility cost if maintainers decide ACPX launch reliability outweighs parallel delegation.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and require live proof
recommendation.body: Keep default distinct-session parallelism and require a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude reproduction before choosing an OpenClaw or ACPX readiness fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the ACP spawn/control-plane behavior introduced in PR #23580, which osolmaz authored and merged.
